articles.body: A record can belong to workspace Alpha when you check it and workspace Beta when you update it. If the UPDATE filters only by record ID, the earlier check no longer protects the write. In the comments on the previous MCP permissions example , arun pointed out this database boundary . That example used an in-memory map. Moving the handler to a database needs one more decision: which rows is the mutation itself allowed to touch? Here is a small SQLite example that makes the gap reproducible, then closes it with a workspace-scoped write.

articles.title: Too big, it explodes. Too small, it crawls.
articles.excerpt: The learning rate, step by step: why one number decides whether training works at all. Backpropagation tells every weight which way to move: its gradient. It doesn't say how far. That's the job of the…
articles.body: The learning rate, step by step: why one number decides whether training works at all. Backpropagation tells every weight which way to move: its gradient. It doesn't say how far. That's the job of the learning rate, written η (eta). Every step of gradient descent is w ← w − η ∇L The gradient comes from the model. The learning rate is a setting you choose, and it is the first one people tune. This article shows what it does on the smallest possible example, why there is a hard limit on how big it can be, and how practitioners pick it and change it during training. The ideas follow the CS878 Deep Learning lecture on learning rates. One weight on a bowl Take a single weight and the loss L(w) = w², a bowl with its bottom at w = 0.

articles.title: Ofrenda: An altar where dead open-source repos come back to talk
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Every developer has a graveyard. The library you loved in 2014. The framework your first job ran on. Th…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Every developer has a graveyard. The library you loved in 2014. The framework your first job ran on. The tiny utility that did one thing perfectly until its last commit, years ago, quietly said goodbye. Ofrenda is an altar for them. In Mexico, on Día de Muertos, families build an ofrenda : photos, marigolds, candles and the things the dead loved, so their spirits can find their way home for a night. I wanted the same for the code we have lost. You paste the URL of an abandoned GitHub repository and Ofrenda: Opens the grave.

articles.title: Stop Controlling, Start Leading: The "Let Them" Mindset at Work
articles.excerpt: The "Let Them" mindset, popularized by author and speaker Mel Robbins, is one of the simplest mental tools for managing stress. Her premise is straightforward: when people act in ways you do not like…
articles.body: The "Let Them" mindset , popularized by author and speaker Mel Robbins, is one of the simplest mental tools for managing stress. Her premise is straightforward: when people act in ways you do not like or expect, instead of burning energy trying to control them, you step back and say, "Let them." If your team member misses a deadline, let them. If a cross-functional peer pushes back on your strategy, let them. If a executive disagrees with your proposal, let them. At first glance, this sounds like bad advice for a leader. Isn't a manager’s job specifically to direct, correct, and ensure accountability? The answer lies in understanding what "Let Them" actually means in a professional setting. It is not about passive disengagement or ignoring poor work.
articles.author: Debashish Ghosal

articles.title: KILLCHAIN: Following Trust Through the Software Supply Chain
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge. A Hacktoberfest 2026 adventure: Creating KILLCHAIN. We use packages every day. A quick npm command. An import statement. We are using someone'…
articles.body: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge . A Hacktoberfest 2026 adventure: Creating KILLCHAIN. We use packages every day. A quick npm command. An import statement. We are using someone's code. The code that lives in a developer's GitHub repository and the package you download from npm are not always the same. Builds can change files. Sometimes unintended changes end up in the published package. So how do you know that what you are installing is what the developers actually wanted to publish? At the Hacktoberfest Hack Day in Sonipat we found a problem that asked this question directly. It became KILLCHAIN . What We Created KILLCHAIN is a tool that checks whether the published package matches the source code. Enter a package name and a version.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
